text:
alex kim: Heads-up — running a small canary of v3-int8. We're seeing lots of tiny regressions across many slices (0.5–2% each) that don't trip per-slice thresholds but sum up to noticeable quality drift downstream. Proposing a 'cumulative delta watchdog' that aggregates per-slice deltas over a sliding window and triggers an autofallback when the cumulative exceeds a threshold. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

maria gonzalez: can you define how the aggregation works? sum of absolute deltas? weighted by traffic?

alex kim: good q. Idea is: for each slice i compute delta_i = baseline_metric_i - variant_metric_i (could be signed), then cumulative = sum(weight_i * max(0, delta_i)) over slices for last N minutes. trigger if cumulative > T. weight_i = traffic_share_i to bias high-volume slices. Use p95 delta for each slice to avoid noise.

ben chou: p95 makes sense. also cap per-slice contribution so a single noisy slice can't dominate (e.g. cap at 3x slice baseline).

sophia liu: need to combine with latency SLOs — if int8 lowers quality slightly but reduces latency a lot, we might accept more cumulative delta. propose a tunable utility function: utility = alpha * latency_gain - beta * cumulative_delta. fallback if utility < 0.

tara patel: love the control. can we sketch a config snippet for the rollout engine so ops can implement quickly? also suggest a cooldown/hysteresis (don't flip-flop). :scroll:

alex kim: here's a minimal config prototype (pseudo-JSON):

```
{
  "watchdog": "cumulative-delta",
  "window_minutes": 30,
  "slice_aggregation": "weighted_sum",
  "slice_weight_source": "traffic_share",
  "per_slice_cap": 0.03,            // max 3% contribution
  "delta_quantile": 95,             // use p95 per-slice delta
  "trigger_threshold": 0.015,       // 1.5% cumulative weighted delta
  "cooldown_minutes": 30,
  "hysteresis_margin": 0.5          // require 50% drop below threshold to re-enable
}
```

ben chou: nit: make trigger_threshold tunable per-customer tier. enterprise tolerances differ. also log both signed and absolute cumulative for debugging.

maria gonzalez: I'll run a simulated sweep over historical traffic slices with this config and report expected false-positive rate. ETA a few hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sophia liu: Add a composite metric option: cumulative_delta could be sum over multiple fidelity measures (mrr_loss + kl_div * weight). better than single metric.

alex kim: good call. will add multi-metric support. question for infra: can the routing layer expose per-slice traffic_share in real time to the watcher? @infra-bot

infra-bot: routing-metrics: per-slice traffic_shares are available via /metrics/slices and exported to datadog every 60s. Can create a dedicated 10s export if needed.

tara patel: ops playbook items: 1) dashboard with cumulative_delta, per-slice top contributors, utility score; 2) alert channel + runbook; 3) automatic rollback window + manual override. I'll open tickets.

ben chou: also add a "graceful degrade" path: when cumulative passes threshold, route x% traffic to fallback instead of full rollback, for quick signal gathering. canary->50% fallback->full rollback.

maria gonzalez: sim finished — with current thresholds (1.5% trigger, p95, 30m window) false trigger rate on last 30 days ~0.8% per-week. If we relax to 2.0% it's ~0.2% per-week. Results attached to the ticket I'll make.

alex kim: awesome, thanks @maria. I'll draft a PR to rollout-service with the config and a test harness (will include ben's partial fallback flow). tagging @tara for runbook once PR lands.

tara patel: please include an example dashboard widget query and the Datadog alert rule. I'll pair on the runbook. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary run for v3-int8 at 1744448800. Health checks configured: latency p95, cumulative_delta watchdog, error-rate.

alex kim: cool — ping me when the canary finishes. I'll watch the top contributors and be ready to revert. :eyes:

sophia liu: one last ask — record the decision criteria in the model registry entry for v3-int8 (fields: watchdog_config, expected_fpr, simulation_links).

alex kim: will do. cc @maria @ben for review.

tara patel: moving to action items. thanks everyone. :rocket:
